messages.content: Can you predict the price of a house with an area of 2500 square feet, 3 rooms, constructed in the year 2000, and located in New York, and then compare it with the price of a similar house but with an area of 3000 square feet, constructed in the year 2005, and located in Los Angeles? Finally, predict the price of a third house with an area of 2000 square feet, 2 rooms, constructed in the year 1995, and located in Chicago.

function.name: predict_house_price
function.description: Predict house price based on area, number of rooms and year of construction. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

area.description: Area of the house in square feet.

rooms.description: Number of rooms in the house.

year.description: Year when the house was constructed.

location.description: The location or city of the house.

message.reasoning:
We need to call the function twice (or three times). Actually we have two houses first comparison, so we need predictions for each. Then also predict third house.

So total calls: 3 predictions. We'll use the tool "predict_house_price" from functions namespace. Provide arguments accordingly.

We'll produce output after calling. Use correct JSON format. Let's do sequentially:

1st prediction: area=2500, rooms=3, year=2000, location="New York".
2nd prediction: area=3000, rooms=?, they didn't specify rooms; maybe same as previous? They said "similar house". But not specified rooms. We can assume same number of rooms? Might interpret as similar meaning same features except area/year/location. So likely 3 rooms too. I'll ask clarifying? Probably just provide guess. Could set rooms=3. Or could leave unspecified? Must supply all fields. I'd choose 3 rooms.

Third prediction: area=2000, rooms=2, year=1995, location="Chicago".

Let's proceed.
